papers.abstract: We study the interplay between gravitational waves (GWs) from domain wall collapse and the electron electric dipole moment (EDM) in a complex singlet extension of the standard model with dimension-five Yukawa interactions. In this framework, the scalar potential admits CP-related degenerate vacua, leading to the formation of CP domain walls. While the resulting GW signal provides a probe of the vacuum structure of the singlet scalar sector, it does not by itself constitute a CP-violating observable. Once the singlet scalar is coupled to standard model fermions, CP-violating phases become observable through EDMs. We analyze whether current and future EDM experiments can probe the parameter region where the GW signal is detectable by SKA and THEIA. We find that the current electron EDM bound already constrains part of the parameter space, while future sensitivities at the level of $10^{-31}$--$10^{-32}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ can probe regions overlapping with the GW-detectable domain. Our results highlight the complementarity between GW and EDM observables in probing the singlet scalar sector, providing a coherent picture of its vacuum structure and CP properties.

papers.title: $b\to c \bar u q$ decay and $CP$ violating observables in the presence of new physics contributions
papers.abstract: In this work, a comprehensive analysis for processes related to $b\to c\bar{u}q~(q=d, s)$ transitions is carried out, including new physics contributions. In light of a recent tension between branching fractions for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ ($M=π, K$) decays in the QCD factorization approach and relevant experimental results, phenomenological constraints on complex-valued Wilson coefficients are discussed. Analyzed observables contain direct $CP$ asymmetry ($A_{\text{CP}}$) in $B^-\to D^0π^-$ decays and $γ/φ_3$, one of the angles in the unitarity triangle, combined with others from $τ_{B^+}/τ_{B_d}$, $ΔΓ_{q}/Γ_q$, and $A_{\rm SL}^{q}~(q=d, s)$. We constrain the complex Wilson coefficients at $1σ$ and $2σ$ levels under color-singlet and color-rearranged scenarios. These constraints yield correlated predictions for $ΔΓ_d/Γ_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$ and $A_{\text{CP}}$.

papers.title: Probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism with low-frequency gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

papers.title: Mass Varying Neutrino Oscillation in Teleparallel Gravity
papers.abstract: In the Cartan teleparallel formulation of gravity, a scalar field coupled to the torsion tensor can acquire an environment-dependent effective mass. This gives rise to a screening effect: inside dense bodies such as the Sun, the scalar field is suppressed, causing the neutrino mass to vary with local density. We investigate the impact of this torsion-induced screening on solar neutrino oscillations. The mechanism modifies the standard MSW resonance condition distinctly, leading to detectable shifts in the flavor conversion probability. Using data from solar neutrino experiments (Super-Kamiokande, Borexino, SNO), we place constraints on the torsion scalar coupling parameters. Our work provides a concrete test of teleparallel gravity through mass-varying neutrino oscillations.

papers.title: Role of the $Σ(1430)(1/2^-)$ in the $J/ψ\to Λ\barΛ π^0$ reaction
papers.abstract: We study the $J/ψ\to \barΛ Λπ^0$ reaction, an \xiu{isospin-violating} reaction, by looking at the trios of \xiu{a} baryon-antibaryon-pseudoscalar meson that conform to a singlet of $\text{SU}(3)$ in the $u, d, s$ quarks. These terms conserve isospin; however, once the final-state interactions of meson-baryon and meson-antibaryon are taken into account, \xiu{the} isospin is violated due to the different masses of particles within the same isospin multiplets. Since the reaction is tied to the interaction of particles, only resonances that are dynamically generated by these interactions show up in the reaction. In this sense, our approach produces the $Σ(1430)(1/2^-)$ state \xiu{ but not the $Σ(1385)(3/2^+)$ state}. Comparing with the BESIII data we observe that, within the limited statistics of the experiment, the data show a structure {around $M_{πΛ} = 1430$ MeV} that is reproduced by the theory, and no signal is seen for the $Σ(1385)(3/2^+)$ as the theory predicts. We call for a future update of the experiment once better statistics become available.

papers.title: Monopoles, Strings, Walls and Gravitational waves
papers.abstract: The gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2) \to U(1) \to Z_2 \to 1$ successively produces monopoles, strings and domain walls bounded by strings (WBS), with the elementary monopole carrying a $U(1)$ magnetic flux twice as large as the elementary string. The elementary strings and subsequently WBS emit gravitational waves, and during their decay, the WBS yield a network of composite strings that carry the same $U(1)$ flux as the monopoles. Depending on the cosmological evolution, we provide the gravitational wave spectra generated by the elementary strings and WBS, in combination with the composite strings which are either effectively stable, quasistable, or metastable. These three scenarios are also realized in the symmetry breaking chain $SU(3) \to SO(3) \to Z_2 \to 1$. Both $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have appeared in the literature as flavor gauge symmetries.

papers.title: Non-Markovian heavy-quark equilibration and equilibrium correlation function in a thermal medium
papers.abstract: We compute the charm-quark current-current correlation function within the Langevin framework and extract the heavy-quark diffusion coefficient using the Green--Kubo formula. The formalism is further extended to evaluate the correlation function using a generalized Langevin equation that incorporates memory effects via an exponentially decaying memory kernel. We find that while memory effects qualitatively modify the transient structure of the current correlations, the value of the transport coefficient remains unchanged. In addition, we investigate heavy-quark thermalization in the presence of memory and compare the nonequilibrium solution of a generalized Fokker--Planck equation with the one obtained from the generalized Langevin equation in the non-relativistic limit. We also consider the relativistic case with correlated noise and observe that memory effects can give rise to a damped, oscillatory equilibration of the heavy quark momentum distribution in a non-Markovian bath.

papers.title: Photon Fragmentation Functions in LHAPDF: Existing Sets and a Pythia-Based Extraction
papers.abstract: Prompt-photon predictions with experimentally relevant isolation criteria retain a residual dependence on parton-to-photon fragmentation functions, whose phenomenological uncertainties remain only weakly constrained. We present a pragmatic study of photon fragmentation functions extracted from Pythia parton-shower events and stored in LHAPDF grids. We briefly review the role of photon fragmentation in perturbative QCD and then construct shower-level estimates of the flavour-dependent functions $D^{\mathrm{PS}}_{γ/i}(z,μ_D)$ as functions of the photon momentum fraction $z$ and fragmentation scale $μ_D$. The extracted distributions show the expected qualitative hierarchy between quark and gluon channels and an increasing fragmentation contribution with scale. In parallel, we convert the commonly used BFG, GRV, and GDRG parameterizations into LHAPDF grids and study their interpolation. We find that the default logcubic interpolation in LHAPDF reproduces the non-trivial $z$- and scale-dependence of the tabulated fragmentation functions more faithfully than the linear interpolation commonly used in legacy implementations. We also define a simple collider-oriented envelope set, based on the BFG and GRV families. These results provide a portable baseline for future phenomenological studies and for more systematic extractions of photon fragmentation functions.

papers.title: Probing the Inert Scalar Sector of the Inert Doublet Model via Vector-Boson Fusion at a Muon Collider
papers.abstract: We investigate how a future high-energy muon collider (MuC) probe the inert scalar sector of the Inert Doublet Model (IDM) through a comprehensive set of $2\to4$ electroweak gauge-boson fusion processes. The scalar spectrum consists of two $CP$-even neutral scalars, $h$ and $H$, one $CP$-odd neutral scalar $A$, and a pair of charged scalars $H^\pm$. We assume the neutral scalar $H$ is the lightest inert state and the dark matter (DM) candidate, while we identify the observed $125$~GeV Higgs boson with the scalar from the Standard-Model-like doublet. We consider charged Higgs pair production, $μ^+μ^-\to H^+H^-ν\barν$, induced by $WW$ fusion, as well as the associated channels $μ^+μ^-\to HH^\pmμ^\mpν$ and $μ^+μ^-\to AH^\pmμ^\mpν$, induced by $WZ$ and $Wγ$ fusion. Owing to their Vector Boson Fusion (VBF) origin, the corresponding cross sections increase significantly with collider energy, making them particularly well suited for exploration at a high-energy MuC. We first study the $2\to 2$ subprocesses $WW\to H^+ H^-$ and $WV\to H^+ S_i$, with $V=Z, γ$ and $S_i=H,A$, and establish the presence of destructive interference among the contributing diagrams. After imposing theoretical consistency requirements and current experimental constraints, including those from DM and collider searches, we evaluate the corresponding signal rates at $\sqrt{s}=3$, $10$, and $20$~TeV. We further perform a detector-level Monte Carlo analysis combined with a cut-based signal-background selection. Our results demonstrate that the sensitivity to inert scalar production grows significantly with collision energy, establishing the $10$ and $20$~TeV stages of a MuC as powerful probes of the IDM scalar sector.

papers.title: Bakamjian--Thomas construction and light-front zero modes in pseudoscalar transitions: A comparison with the covariant Bethe--Salpeter model
papers.abstract: We examine the role of light-front zero modes in the extraction of the semileptonic form factor $f_-(q^2)$ between pseudoscalar mesons. In an exactly solvable covariant Bethe--Salpeter (BS) model, we calculate the transverse-current zero-mode contribution directly from the shrinking nonvalence region and reproduce it with an effective operator in the valence convolution. In the valence-only light-front quark model (LFQM) based on the Bakamjian--Thomas (BT) construction, the one-body current is built from on-shell constituent spinors, and the interaction enters through the mass operator and wave functions. The $(+,\perp)$ extraction of $f_-$ is zero-mode free and is saturated by the on-shell overlap. Using the free constituent invariant masses in the internal minus-current projection gives the same $f_-$ from $(+,-)$ after integration. For spacelike momentum transfer, we prove this equality for rotationally invariant radial wave functions with the light-front Jacobian and the adopted pseudoscalar spin coupling, provided the reduced overlaps converge. Subtracting the minus-current result obtained with physical meson masses from the common transverse result gives the BT completion. Current-component independence indirectly identifies this completion as the effective zero-mode contribution missing from the physical-mass minus-current extraction. When the BS valence current and the effective zero-mode operator for the nonvalence endpoint contribution are transferred unchanged to the Gaussian BT-based LFQM, the resulting expression fails to reproduce the component-independent BT result for $f_-$. We construct a mass-weighted complex transverse contour on which the Gaussian wave functions remain analytic for $0<q^2<(m_1+m_2)^2$, where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the initial and final active-quark masses.

papers.title: Mass and decay angles in the $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
papers.abstract: We compare three definitions of $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing within a constituent-quark model: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the two operator-based definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The operator-based angles are closer to the lattice determinations $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$, but remain larger. We then couple conventional $qsQ$ states to virtual $qsQg$ configurations, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. An orbital-$S$-wave chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability stays below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. Eliminating the hybrid sector gives a rank-one mass correction precisely when all weighted transitions select the same retained-state combination. The mode-resolved calculation separates the flavor-breaking response that changes the mixing angle from the response that generates a second transition direction. The accompanying effective-current relation connects this mass analysis to radiative and semileptonic amplitudes through their current matrix elements.

papers.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
papers.abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

papers.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
papers.abstract: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969, and Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form and supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The cascade description has five predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) assembles these pieces into HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions, and fits it to the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, local strangeness balance, and forward resonance signals.

papers.title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
papers.abstract: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $Δm^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $Δm^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $ν_μ$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$, and the $ν_μ$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $θ_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy range, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|Δm^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $δ_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$ and $θ_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.

papers.title: $X(2370)$ without exceptionalism from reanalyzing $J/ψ\to γ+ 3P$ data
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/ψ$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/ψ\toγPPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0η^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $η(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $η_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0η$ and $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: Two-dimensional Pulsar Distance Inference from Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are limited in localizing nanohertz continuous gravitational waves (CGWs) by uncertainties in pulsar distances. We introduce a method to infer pulsar distances in two dimensions, using phase information from the pulsar terms of multiple CGW sources. Our approach can enhance distance precision relative to existing one-dimensional distance-inference methods. Using idealized SKA-motivated PTA simulations with prospective pulsar-distance priors, we combine information from five high-SNR CGW sources with known sky positions and luminosity distances. For example, our method achieves subparsec precision for a simulated pulsar at $0.8\,\mathrm{kpc}$ in $40\%$ of realizations, compared with none for the existing one-dimensional method. Such improvements in pulsar-distance precision could facilitate CGW host-galaxy identification and multimessenger observational prospects.

papers.title: Hadron properties at finite temperature
papers.abstract: This review provides an overview of thermal effects on hadron properties, focusing on the theoretical frameworks used to describe in-medium modifications of masses, decay widths, and spectral functions. We examine the application of finite-temperature quantum field theory---specifically the imaginary-time formalism (ITF)---to analyze both light- and heavy-hadron sectors. For light hadrons, we discuss the role of chiral symmetry restoration and the different definitions of thermal masses in effective field theories, like chiral perturbation theory. In the heavy-flavor sector, we review recent progress in describing open-heavy mesons and quarkonia using self-consistent unitarized approaches and nonrelativistic effective field theories. All these results are complemented by analyses of recent lattice-QCD calculations using the Euclidean formulation of QCD at finite temperature, relevant to extracting screening masses and reconstructing spectral functions. Finally, we discuss the phenomenological impact of the thermal modifications on experimental observables in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, including numerical simulations, dilepton spectra, transport coefficients, and hadron femtoscopy. By combining phenomenological considerations with robust theoretical tools, this review provides a coherent picture of how thermal effects emerge in the hadronic phase and how they can be systematically studied within controlled frameworks. Ultimately, the discussion serves as a bridge between experimental observations in relativistic heavy-ion collisions and fundamental developments in finite-temperature QCD and effective field theories for hadronic systems.

papers.title: Perturbations in the parametrized wormhole spacetime and their related quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: We study electromagnetic perturbations and the associated quasinormal modes (QNMs) of parametrized static, spherically symmetric wormhole spacetimes, focusing on Damour-Solodukhin and braneworld geometries as well as their galactic extensions. Using the Bronnikov-Konoplya-Pappas (BKP) parametrization, we express the metric functions in terms of a compactified radial coordinate and characterize the spacetime through far-field and near-throat parameters. The far-field coefficients govern the asymptotic structure and post-Newtonian behaviour, while the near-throat continued-fraction expansion captures the strong-field geometry near the throat. We first apply the parametrization to isolated wormholes and identify its range of validity, showing that the non-analytic metric functions can limit the applicability of the BKP scheme. Moreover we have shown that such issues can indeed hamper the primary ringdown waveform. We then extend the framework to a galactic Damour-Solodukhin wormhole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo. Imposing observational bounds from the shadow of Sgr A$^*$, we constrain the galactic compactness and deformation parameters and obtain an observationally viable parametrized metric. Within the allowed parameter space, we compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the transfer matrix method and analyze the corresponding time-domain ringdown signals. We find that the damping rate is more sensitive to galactic compactness, whereas the oscillation frequency remains comparatively stable. Although the spectral shifts are small within the shadow-allowed region, the framework provides a systematic link between geometric parametrization, shadow constraints, and dynamical response. Our results establish an observationally consistent parametrized description of wormhole perturbations for strong-field tests of horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Superconducting Cosmic Strings
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of superconducting cosmic-string networks in a $U(1)_{\rm local}\times U(1)_{\rm global}$ field-theoretic model using three-dimensional lattice field simulations in an expanding universe. The scalar field charged under $U(1)_{\rm local}$ forms cosmic strings, while the scalar field associated with $U(1)_{\rm global}$ acts as a current carrier and condenses in their vicinity. We investigate the evolution of the string network for several values of the coupling constant between the string-forming and current-carrier fields and estimate the gravitational-wave power spectrum sourced by the resulting superconducting cosmic-string network. We find that the spectral shape depends on the coupling constant: as the interaction strength increases, the spectrum is suppressed on small scales. This feature may be probed by future high-frequency gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: Multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: Angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
papers.abstract: The angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated M1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses and mass ratios. The main analysis is restricted to merger remnants that do not collapse to a black hole within the simulated time intervals. The angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. Following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. The dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. The degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. Superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. The associated half frequency, $f_{\mathrm{dom}}/2\simeq0.6$--$0.7\,\mathrm{kHz}$, is compared with local rotation rates in the simulated remnant--disk systems, suggesting a possible dynamical association between the remnant structure and neutrino variability. Finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. The polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron rich and below equilibrium.

papers.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
papers.abstract: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.
